text:
sara_support: FYI escalation from ACME — they're seeing p99 jump ~400ms around 2026-03-17 09:12 UTC. They say their workload is pinned to eu-west-1 but trace shows a handoff to us-east. Pasting the trace they sent:

sara_support: ```
trace_id: acme-20260317-09:12-xyz
client -> acme-proxy-eu (10.10.5.12) -> redwood-edge-eu (10.20.5.3) -> redwood-egress-eu -> transit -> redwood-egress-us-east (34.80.2.11) -> model-us-east1
observed_latency_ms: 412 (tokenization step)
notes: x-rw-region header = eu-west-1 present on request
```

jamal_oncall: looking into it now. I can reproduce a p99 tail from our test tenant when I force region header. Quick probe: 

jamal_oncall: ```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "x-rw-region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rw-serving-region: us-east-1
x-rw-route-id: fallback-multi-v2
content-length: 0
```

jamal_oncall: so the service is returning a us-east serve header even though client asked eu-west. :eyes:

ivan_runtime: that smells like the passive fallback routing policy kicked in. We shipped a small canary yesterday that loosens the datacenter affinity threshold when local capacity < 15%. If the eu pool dipped, the router may have auto-failed to a compatible variant in us-east.

ivan_runtime: can you paste the exact route metadata for that account (route-id + model tag)? I want to confirm compatibility matrix.

sara_support: route id from ACME's request: `acct/acme/route/rl-92f` model tag: `open-moss:1.3-quant` they insisted they had reserved dedicated eu instances though.

katie_network: adding network perspective — we have a brief peering flap at 09:10 UTC on eqp-ams-2 (see netlogs). Some eBGP withdraws caused traffic to prefer a transatlantic path for ~3m. That could explain why traffic exited via our us-east egress.

katie_network: mitigations: 1) re-enable stronger region stickiness for that account, 2) evaluate peering route dampening for eqp-ams-2. Quick sticky override cmd is below.

katie_network: ```
# apply sticky region override for the account route
/routing override --account acme --route rl-92f --sticky-region eu-west-1 --ttl 24h
```

sara_support: can we do the sticky override now? ACME is on a call.

ops-bot: routing override  queued: id=or-7741, owner=katie_network

deploy-bot: routing override or-7741 applied to rl-92f (eu-west-1) by katie_network at 2026-03-17T09:18:12Z

jamal_oncall: monitoring metrics now — p99 for the ACME key dropped from 410ms -> 120ms within two minutes of the override. Still watching for regressions.

ivan_runtime: follow-up actions: we should revert the canary loosen once we confirm the eu capacity calculations are stable. I'll open a PR to tighten the threshold and add an alert when egress-drift > 5% for pinned accounts.

sara_support: noted. I'll tell ACME the immediate fix (sticky override) was applied and we're rolling a code change to prevent accidental cross-region fallback for pinned dedicated customers.

jamal_oncall: thumbs up. I'll keep a 30m watch on p99 and the egress metrics for acme account. :thumbsup:

sara_support: thanks all. ACME on the call said latency looks normal now. Closing for now but keeping postmortem on the incident board.
